feed.title: Handling PQ signatures on the stack

entry.title: Handling PQ signatures on the stack
entry.summary:
Restricting the use of opcodes, specifically `OP_DUP`, to operate only on stack elements less than or equal to 520 bytes, introduces noteworthy changes in how scripts are constructed and executed. By imposing such a limitation, it becomes necessary for the witness to include the relevant stack element twice if equivalent functionality is desired. In effect, this approach shifts the burden to the spender, who must now bear the cost associated with the increased witness size.
Although `OP_EQUAL` can be utilized to verify that two large stack elements are identical, its behavior presents a significant drawback. Upon execution, `OP_EQUAL` consumes both input elements by popping them from the stack. Consequently, after confirming their equality, no further operations can be performed on these elements since they are no longer available within the stack context. This aspect restricts the versatility typically afforded by `OP_DUP`, especially when subsequent manipulations of the duplicated data are required.
